overview: News Corporation is a global media and information services company operating through five segments: Dow Jones (business/financial news and data), Digital Real Estate Services (majority-owned REA Group in Australia plus Move/realtor.com in the US), Book Publishing (HarperCollins), News Media (mastheads including the New York Post, The Sun, The Times/Sunday Times, and Australian titles), and Other. Following the April 2025 completion of the Foxtel divestiture to DAZN, News Corp has shifted toward a higher-margin, more digital and subscription/data-driven mix anchored by Dow Jones' B2B/Risk & Compliance data business and the two real estate listings portals. The company is controlled by the Murdoch family through a dual-class share structure (Class B super-voting shares), with News Corp's economic interest in the Murdoch Family Trust around 14% but roughly 41% of voting power.

business_model.summary: Revenue is generated from a mix of B2B data/subscription services (Dow Jones Risk & Compliance, Factiva), consumer digital and print subscriptions (WSJ, Barron's, UK/Australian mastheads), real estate listings/marketplace fees (REA Group, realtor.com), book publishing royalties/sales (HarperCollins), digital and print advertising, and a fast-growing new stream of AI content-licensing deals (OpenAI, Meta). The Foxtel pay-TV segment (previously 'Other') was divested in April 2025, removing a capital-intensive, lower-margin subscription TV business and improving consolidated margins and ROIC.

revenue_streams.name: Dow Jones
revenue_streams.detail: WSJ, Barron's, MarketWatch, Factiva, Risk & Compliance, Dow Jones Newswires; FY2026 revenue ~$2,497M, EBITDA ~$663M; management targets $1B segment EBITDA by FY2030

revenue_streams.name: Digital Real Estate Services (REA Group + Move/realtor.com)
revenue_streams.detail: FY2026 revenue ~$2,016M, EBITDA ~$741M (highest-margin segment); REA Group majority-owned Australian listings leader, realtor.com the #2 US portal by visits

revenue_streams.name: Book Publishing (HarperCollins)
revenue_streams.detail: FY2026 revenue ~$2,288M, EBITDA ~$287M; general fiction/nonfiction, children's, Christian publishing (Zondervan, Thomas Nelson), backlist-driven cash flow

revenue_streams.name: News Media
revenue_streams.detail: FY2026 revenue ~$2,227M, EBITDA ~$139M; NY Post, The Sun, The Times/Sunday Times, Australian mastheads, talkSPORT; structural print decline offset by digital subscriptions, licensing and cost discipline

revenue_streams.name: Other (incl. divested Foxtel)
revenue_streams.detail: Foxtel/Kayo/BINGE sold to DAZN, completed April 2025; residual 'Other' now mainly corporate costs, EBITDA ~$(203)M in FY2026

business_model.customer_type: Mixed: B2B subscribers and enterprises (Dow Jones Risk & Compliance, Factiva), consumer subscribers (WSJ, News Media digital), real estate agents/brokers and consumers (REA, realtor.com), retail book buyers, and increasingly AI platform companies as content licensees
business_model.geographic_mix: United States (Dow Jones, HarperCollins, NY Post, realtor.com), Australia (REA Group, Australian mastheads), United Kingdom (The Sun, The Times, talkSPORT), with smaller presence across Europe and Asia

main_competitors: The New York Times Company and Financial Times (business/financial news)
Penguin Random House, Simon & Schuster, Hachette (publishing)
competitive_position.market_position: Dow Jones is a top-tier global business/financial news and data provider with a strong enterprise data moat (Risk & Compliance, Factiva); REA Group is the clear #1 real estate listings portal in Australia; realtor.com/Move is the #2 US real estate portal by site visits (~31% of portal visits vs. Zillow's >50% of visits, but engagement per-user metrics favor realtor.com); HarperCollins is a top-5 global trade publisher; News Media titles hold strong but declining legacy positions in UK/Australia/US tabloid and premium news markets.

moat_factors.description: Risk & Compliance and Factiva are embedded, high-switching-cost data/workflow products sold to financial institutions and corporates, generating recurring, high-margin revenue roughly half of Dow Jones EBITDA

moat_factors.factor: Network effects in real estate listings
moat_factors.description: REA Group and realtor.com benefit from two-sided marketplace dynamics (agents need buyer traffic, buyers need comprehensive listings), though Zillow's larger audience creates a stronger network effect in the US
WSJ, Barron's, HarperCollins imprints, and News Media mastheads are century-old trusted brands now monetizable via AI licensing in addition to traditional subscriptions/advertising
~$250M five-year OpenAI deal and up to $50M/year Meta deal demonstrate a new, largely incremental high-margin revenue stream from proprietary archives, though durability/renewal terms are untested
Shared technology, data and advertising-sales infrastructure across global mastheads provides some cost leverage versus smaller independent publishers

weaknesses: realtor.com/Move trails Zillow by a wide margin in US real estate audience scale and brand recognition
News Media segment faces structural secular print decline (industry-wide double-digit circulation drops) with thin ~6% EBITDA margins
Dual-class share structure concentrates control with the Murdoch family, creating governance overhang and periodic activist pressure (e.g., Starboard Value proposal to collapse the structure)
REA Group, while majority-owned, is a separately listed entity (ASX: REA) — News Corp does not have full economic control and REA's growth is tied to the cyclical Australian housing/listings market
Exposure to AI-driven disintermediation of news discovery and traffic (aggregators/chatbots reducing referral traffic to publisher sites)

growth_drivers: Dow Jones path to $1 billion segment EBITDA by fiscal 2030, driven by Risk & Compliance growth (double-digit), WSJ digital subscriber growth, and B2B data expansion
AI content-licensing deals (OpenAI ~$250M/5-yr, Meta up to $50M/yr) as a new, high-margin, largely incremental revenue stream with potential for additional AI partnerships
Realtor.com market share gains — seven consecutive quarters of YoY revenue growth, improving monetization per visit, and renewed strategic initiatives under Move leadership
REA Group continued pricing power, add-on product penetration, and resilient new-buy listings volumes in the Australian residential market
Margin expansion and capital return acceleration following the Foxtel divestiture, which reduced capital intensity and strengthened the balance sheet (FY2026 buybacks ~4x prior year at $643M)
HarperCollins backlist monetization and potential for further digital/audio format growth
Portfolio simplification/M&A optionality — management has signaled continued focus on higher-margin "core growth pillars" and openness to further non-core divestitures

business.description: Zillow's larger audience and traffic dominance in the US real estate portal market constrains realtor.com's pricing power and growth ceiling despite recent share gains

business.risk: Secular print decline in News Media
business.description: Structural, industry-wide decline in print circulation and advertising; New York Post and other mastheads losing print circulation annually, requiring continued digital transition and cost discipline
Growing exposure to AI chatbots/aggregators reducing referral traffic to publisher websites, potentially offsetting licensing revenue gains
News Corp does not fully control REA Group's strategy or capital allocation despite majority ownership; REA Group itself faces competition from Domain and other portals

financial.description: Significant AUD and GBP revenue/earnings exposure (REA Group, UK titles) versus USD reporting currency

financial.risk: Litigation costs from AI enforcement strategy
financial.description: Ongoing lawsuits against AI platforms (e.g., Perplexity, Brave) for content scraping could be costly and divert management attention even as licensing deals monetize the same content

regulatory.description: GDPR, UK GDPR, CCPA, and Australia's Privacy Act expose the company to potential fines of up to 4% of global turnover for non-compliance across its digital properties
Activist investors (e.g., Starboard Value) have pushed to collapse the dual-class structure; any succession-related governance disputes within the Murdoch Family Trust could create uncertainty

macro.description: Digital Real Estate Services (REA Group and realtor.com) revenue is directly tied to housing transaction volumes and new-listing activity in Australia and the US, both sensitive to interest rates and affordability
News Media and Dow Jones advertising revenues remain sensitive to broader macroeconomic and corporate marketing spend cycles

execution.description: FY2025/FY2026 YoY comparisons are distorted by the April 2025 Foxtel divestiture (gain on sale, DAZN minority stake received); continuing-operations figures should be used for trend analysis

execution.risk: Renewal risk on AI licensing deals
execution.description: OpenAI and Meta deals are multi-year but fixed-term; renewal terms, pricing, and durability of this new revenue stream beyond the initial contract periods are unproven

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Mixed: legacy print news in structural decline industry-wide; digital subscriptions and B2B data/analytics growing; US and Australian real estate listings markets recovering modestly with resilient new-listing volumes; AI licensing emerging as a meaningful new revenue category for premium content owners
macro_factors.cyclicality: Moderate-to-high — Digital Real Estate Services segment is meaningfully cyclical (tied to housing transaction and listing volumes, interest-rate sensitive), while Dow Jones B2B/subscription revenue and HarperCollins backlist sales are comparatively defensive
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Moderate-to-high indirect sensitivity via housing market activity (REA Group, realtor.com) and corporate cost of capital; low direct balance-sheet sensitivity given modest leverage (debt/equity ~0.3x, net debt/EBITDA ~0.6x per most recent data)
macro_factors.currency_exposure: Material AUD exposure (REA Group) and GBP exposure (The Sun, The Times, talkSPORT) translated into USD reporting currency

recent_developments.event: Completed sale of Foxtel Group (pay-TV, Kayo, BINGE) to DAZN for ~$3.4B including repayment of $592M shareholder loans; News Corp received ~6% minority equity stake in DAZN. This materially changes YoY comparability — FY2025 continuing-operations results exclude Foxtel, and headline net income in FY2025 (~$1,340M per filings) reflects a large gain on sale rather than recurring operating profit.
Signed multi-year AI licensing deal with Meta worth up to $50M per year (minimum three years), allowing Meta's AI tools to use News Corp's US/UK archive and current content

Finalized ~$250M, five-year AI content-licensing deal with OpenAI covering WSJ, Barron's, MarketWatch, New York Post, The Times of London, The Sun, and Australian titles — the largest publisher deal in OpenAI's roster

Reported record Q4 FY2026 results: revenue +11% to $2.3B, total segment EBITDA +31% to $423M, net income +167% YoY (continuing ops) to $230M, adjusted EPS $0.35 vs $0.19 prior year; FY2026 operating cash flow +26% to $1.24B and FY margin improved from 16.7% to 18%
Share buybacks accelerated to ~4x the prior year's pace, totaling $643M for FY2026 ($184M in Q4 alone); management stated it believes the stock is materially undervalued
New York Post expanded into the Los Angeles market with the launch of 'California Post', incurring incremental near-term costs that modestly pressured News Media segment EBITDA

Realtor.com posted its seventh consecutive quarter of YoY revenue growth with Q4 FY2026 revenue +13%, while REA Group revenue rose 21% aided by pricing increases, add-on products, and an 11% rise in Australian residential new-buy listings

Activist investor Starboard Value filed a non-binding proposal urging News Corp to collapse its dual-class share structure, intensifying scrutiny of Murdoch family control (~14% economic interest, ~41% voting power) amid broader Murdoch family succession planning discussions

items.notes: Longer-term goal reiterated on recent earnings calls, driven by Risk & Compliance growth, digital subscriber gains, and AI licensing contributions
Management stated early signs for Q1 FY2027 are 'certainly positive' and expects FY2026's momentum (margin expansion from 16.7% to 18%) to carry forward, with further margin expansion expected
FY2026 buybacks of $643M were ~4x the prior year's pace; management explicitly stated belief that the stock is materially undervalued, signaling intent to sustain elevated buyback activity
Expectation of continued realtor.com market-share gains and REA Group pricing/add-on product growth, subject to housing market conditions

guidance.management_commentary: CEO Robert Thomson and Chair Lachlan Murdoch emphasized that Dow Jones, Digital Real Estate Services, and Book Publishing ('core growth pillars') continue to generate outsized performance, with expanding AI licensing partnerships (OpenAI, Meta) and Realtor.com share gains cited as key opportunities. Management does not provide formal quantitative revenue/EPS guidance ranges in press releases but has reiterated the FY2030 Dow Jones $1B EBITDA target and signaled confidence in continued margin expansion and capital returns given a strengthened balance sheet post-Foxtel sale.

bull_case: Post-Foxtel portfolio is leaner, higher-margin, and less capital intensive, with accelerating free cash flow (FY2026 operating cash flow +26% to $1.24B) funding aggressive buybacks management views as highly accretive given perceived undervaluation

AI content-licensing deals (OpenAI ~$250M/5yr, Meta up to $50M/yr) represent a new, largely incremental high-margin revenue stream that validates the value of News Corp's proprietary content archives and could expand with further deals
Dow Jones' B2B/Risk & Compliance data business provides durable, recurring, high-margin revenue with a credible path to $1B segment EBITDA by FY2030, reducing reliance on cyclical advertising

Realtor.com has posted seven consecutive quarters of YoY growth and is gaining engagement share (visits-per-user) even as it trails Zillow in raw traffic, suggesting room for continued monetization improvement
REA Group provides exposure to a structurally advantaged, high-margin Australian real estate listings monopoly-like business with pricing power and resilient demand
bear_case: News Media segment faces unrelenting structural print decline with thin margins (~6% EBITDA margin in FY2026) that could continue to be a drag even as digital subscriptions grow
Realtor.com remains a distant #2 to Zillow in US real estate portal traffic/audience scale, limiting its ceiling for market share and pricing power versus the incumbent leader

Dual-class share structure and concentrated Murdoch family control (via ~41% voting power on a ~14% economic stake) creates governance risk, limits minority shareholder influence, and has drawn activist pressure (Starboard Value) and succession-related uncertainty

Digital Real Estate Services earnings are meaningfully exposed to housing market cyclicality in both the US and Australia, making a chunk of News Corp's growth engine sensitive to interest-rate and macro shocks

AI licensing revenue, while currently a tailwind, carries renewal risk beyond initial contract terms and could be partly offset by AI-driven disintermediation of traditional publisher traffic and advertising over time
